inspection_summary: Complete inspection of all 429 normalized lines. The paper turns long-time escape from a one- or two-hole circular billiard into arithmetic sums over near-periodic trajectories, rewrites the small-hole asymptotics through Mellin transforms and Dirichlet L-functions, states escape-rate criteria equivalent to RH and related to GRH, treats irrational hole separation by a mean-field argument, and uses numerical figures to test convergence and the role of complex poles. The extraction interleaves two PDF columns and damages several displayed formulas and tables, so accepted claims are limited to mathematics recoverable from the accompanying prose and exact formula normalizations are flagged for later scan verification.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the proposed experimental comparison of one- and two-hole escape and its expression through zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

sections_inspected.label: Physical motivation and circle-billiard model
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contrasts integrable and chaotic escape laws, defines the circle map, distinguishes periodic from equidistributed trajectories, and specifies invariant measure, holes, and escape time.

sections_inspected.label: Periodic-orbit survival and Mellin representation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies near-periodic trajectories as the long-time survivors, integrates their phase-space neighborhoods, compresses the orbit sum with the Ramanujan identity, and introduces Mellin inversion for small-hole asymptotics.

sections_inspected.label: Rational separation and character reduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Splits orbit periods into residue classes, uses Dirichlet-character orthogonality and Euler products, and obtains the rational two-hole Mellin integrand in terms of L-functions.

sections_inspected.label: Residues, RH/GRH criteria, and irrational separation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Specializes rational configurations, states RH-equivalent escape limits, relates rational corrections to GRH, explains the irrational-angle obstruction, and derives its leading mean-field term.

sections_inspected.label: Numerical checks, conclusion, and back matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reports scaling and residue-truncation tests, separates the roles of real and critical-line poles, summarizes scope, and closes with applications, acknowledgments, and references.

accepted_units.title: One-versus-two-hole escape as a probe of internal dynamics
accepted_units.why_material: The abstract proposes a directly comparable experimental observable whose exact circle-billiard formulas are sums over zeta zeros, establishing the paper's bridge from escape dynamics to RH.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a programmatic claim; the derivation and precise limits occur later in the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low for the prose claim; the two-column layout is visually interleaved but the abstract remains recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Escape-law contrast and the short-time masking confound
accepted_units.why_material: The source contrasts power-law survival in an integrable billiard with exponential survival in a strongly chaotic one and warns that a transient exponential contribution can mask the integrable asymptotic in simulations.
accepted_units.context_note: The coefficient called an escape rate here is the coefficient of the long-time power law, not an exponential decay constant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low for the prose; left- and right-column sentences are interleaved on each normalized line.

accepted_units.title: Circle map, orbit dichotomy, invariant measure, and hole observable
accepted_units.why_material: The unit-radius circle map preserves the collision angle, rational angle choices give equally spaced periodic collisions, irrational choices are uniformly distributed around the boundary, and holes convert these dynamics into a survival-time observable under an invariant boundary measure.
accepted_units.context_note: The two holes are boundary intervals beginning at 0 and theta; theta=0 is the one-hole case, and continuous escape time is collision count times the free-flight time.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the prose is clear, but beta, psi, interval endpoints, and the map are formula-bearing and should be checked against the retained PDF before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Ramanujan compression of the periodic-orbit escape sum
accepted_units.why_material: After defining the positive-part square function, the source rewrites trigonometric orbit contributions as exponentials and applies the Ramanujan identity, replacing a sum over coprime phases by Möbius and totient weights in the long-time coefficient.
accepted_units.context_note: The relevant periods are restricted by the hole width, and the result is the finite coefficient denoted P-infinity in equation (4).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the prose securely supports the Ramanujan-to-Möbius mechanism, but the displayed definition and equation (4) are column-interleaved and require scan verification for exact constants and arguments.

accepted_units.title: Near-periodic trajectories control long-time survival
accepted_units.why_material: The source argues that exact non-escape is confined to certain short periodic orbits and that very long finite survival comes from slow precession near them; it parameterizes the angular deviation, describes the surviving boundary intervals, and integrates their invariant measure to obtain the leading 1/t contribution.
accepted_units.context_note: The normalized span also contains the parallel right-column arithmetic derivation; the trajectory argument is read down the left column and culminates in the displayed asymptotic near lines 150-154.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the geometric mechanism is prose-recoverable, while the interval formula, modular notation, and final normalization are damaged by two-column extraction and need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Mellin inversion converts small-hole behavior into a residue problem
accepted_units.why_material: The finite, piecewise-smooth long-time coefficient is Mellin transformed in hole width, the orbit sum is interchanged with the integral in a convergence half-plane, and inverse Mellin integration makes the small-hole expansion a sum of residues.
accepted_units.context_note: The fractional-part weights depend on theta; the closing lines introduce rational theta=2pi r/q as the case where those weights become residue-class data.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the transform-and-residue strategy is explicit in prose, but equations (4)-(5), powers, and prefactors should be verified from the retained page image.

accepted_units.title: Rational hole separation becomes residue-class harmonic analysis
accepted_units.why_material: For rational theta, the orbit-period sum splits by congruence classes modulo q; dividing by the class gcd produces coprime reduced data, and Dirichlet-character orthogonality acts as the projector selecting a residue class.
accepted_units.context_note: The definitions of reduced a-prime and q-prime and the character convention that vanishes off the units modulo q-prime are part of the required setup.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium-high: the group and orthogonality prose is clear, but primes, congruences, and the displayed delta identity need scan verification because columns and symbols are interleaved.

accepted_units.title: Euler products turn the congruence sum into Dirichlet L-function ratios
accepted_units.why_material: Inserting character orthogonality permits a sum over all integers; prime factorization then separates the totient and Möbius contributions into Euler factors, yielding a character sum involving L(s,chi) over L(s+1,chi). The trivial character recovers zeta with factors at primes dividing the modulus removed.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit supplies the arithmetic engine used in the exact rational two-hole Mellin formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: prose supports the factorization and L-function relationship, but equations (9)-(13) are visibly fragmented; exact Euler factors, powers, and normalizations must be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Exact rational two-hole escape as residues of an L-function integrand
accepted_units.why_material: The first main result expresses the long-time two-hole survival coefficient as residues of a Mellin integrand assembled from congruence data and Dirichlet L-functions, and justifies shifting the contour left by controlling large negative real and imaginary parts.
accepted_units.context_note: Here theta=2pi r/q, with b, a-prime, and q-prime defined by gcd reduction; poles arise through the displayed formula (14), including its L(s+1,chi) denominator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the theorem's conceptual content and contour conditions are recoverable from prose, but the exact residue formula is split across columns and must be scan-verified before symbolic use.

accepted_units.title: RH as a small-hole escape asymptotic
accepted_units.why_material: The source states that RH is equivalent to two families of nested limits: one compares one-hole survival with its leading 2/epsilon term, and the other compares one-hole survival with twice the symmetric two-hole survival, with errors tested against every positive delta.
accepted_units.context_note: P1 and P2 denote the one-hole and symmetric two-hole problems, and the time limit is taken before the small-hole limit in the displayed criteria (15)-(16).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the prose explicitly asserts equivalence, but the precise epsilon exponent, factors, and order of limits should be checked against the retained PDF because the equations share lines with a damaged table.

accepted_units.title: Rational GRH corrections versus the irrational-angle analytic barrier
accepted_units.why_material: For rational two-hole separation, the source relates correction size to generalized RH for the participating L-functions; for irrational separation it says the residue-class analysis breaks down and proposes that dense critical-line poles obstruct analytic continuation, while retaining a theta-independent leading term.
accepted_units.context_note: The density of poles is presented as a presumption, not a proved result; the leading irrational term is developed separately by averaging.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the comparison is prose-recoverable; exact correction exponents and the damaged table entries require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Mean-field averaging for irrational hole separation
accepted_units.why_material: Uniform distribution of the fractional parts for irrational theta permits averaging the hole-overlap weight, while mean values for the totient and Möbius functions replace the remaining arithmetic factors; the resulting integral gives the leading tP(t) approximately equal to 1/epsilon.
accepted_units.context_note: The source claims this leading term is theta-independent for theta greater than zero; it does not extend the rational analytic continuation argument to irrational theta.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the averaging logic and final leading term are explicit in prose, but equations (17)-(18) and their constants are interleaved with corrupted table material and should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Residue hierarchy separates hole geometry from zeta-zero corrections
accepted_units.why_material: The source identifies the leading inverse-hole-width residue with total hole size, explains the vanishing candidate constant term, records special logarithmic and simple integer-pole terms, and places the next-order contributions at nontrivial zeros of zeta, yielding its RH condition on their real parts.
accepted_units.context_note: The especially simple rational separations q=1,2,3,4,6 involve only zeta according to the source; q=6 has a double-pole epsilon log epsilon term.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the qualitative pole taxonomy is supported by prose, while table values, residue constants, multiplicity powers, and the extracted square-root artifact need verification from the original page.

accepted_units.title: Complex poles are required for the survival function's step structure
accepted_units.why_material: The numerical discussion observes that retaining only real poles would produce an analytic integer-power series, whereas complex poles are essential to reconstruct the nonanalytic step structure of the exact finite orbit sum.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a representation-level explanation tied to convergence of the residue expansion, not a separate proof of RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-medium: the prose claim is clear; its visual manifestation is deferred to figure 4.

accepted_units.title: Scaled survival collapse tests the irrational leading asymptotic
accepted_units.why_material: Figure 3 varies the hole width with fixed irrational separation and reports that epsilon times tP(t) approaches a limiting curve in the scaled time epsilon t, converging to one at large scaled time as predicted by equation (18).
accepted_units.context_note: The caption reports 10^8 random initial conditions and theta=1; this is evidence about convergence behavior, while the paper's main formulas are described as exact.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the caption is recoverable, but the plotted curves and uncertainty cannot be reconstructed from normalized text alone.

accepted_units.title: Pole truncation separates smooth convergence from visible steps
accepted_units.why_material: Figure 4 varies the number of critical-line poles in the residue computation and reports convergence of the second derivative, with more real poles needed in one inverse-width regime and more critical poles needed in another for the steps to become visible.
accepted_units.context_note: The caption relates the uniformly spaced steps and constant average gradient back to the exact finite-sum expression (4).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium-high: the caption supports the convergence logic, but axes, curve values, and the damaged derivative label require inspection of the retained figure.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From integrable rotations to L-function poles
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source's central chain passes from conserved-angle circle dynamics to near-periodic survivor measure, then from a finite arithmetic orbit sum through Mellin inversion and character Euler products to residues governed by Dirichlet L-functions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The extracted displays do not safely preserve every constant or Euler factor, so this synthesis supports the mechanism but requires scan verification for a symbolic reconstruction.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One-hole versus symmetric two-hole cancellation isolates RH-sensitive corrections
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Removing the leading geometric hole-size contribution by either subtraction in the one-hole case or comparison with twice the symmetric two-hole case leaves a correction whose stated small-hole bound is equivalent to RH.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is the paper's stated equivalence for its exact escape model; it is not independent evidence that RH is true, and the precise displayed limit must be checked against the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Rational and irrational separations require different arithmetic representations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Rational separation supports finite residue-class decomposition and Dirichlet-character analysis, whereas irrational separation is treated only at leading order through equidistribution and mean values after the source says the analytic continuation route breaks down.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The proposed density of critical-line poles in the irrational case is explicitly speculative, and the mean-field calculation does not recover the full correction structure.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Pole content controls both asymptotic order and visible nonsmoothness
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Integer poles organize leading geometric and analytic terms, while nontrivial complex poles control RH-sensitive corrections and are needed to reproduce the exact escape coefficient's step structure; the figures test convergence in these two representations.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The normalized text retains captions but not an inspectable rendering of the curves, so the reported numerical behavior cannot be independently quantified here.
